In this lesson we will sort out who has to get a Missouri license, including residents and people who have just moved here. Then we will look at the short list of people who do not need one, such as members of the armed forces and full-time students. Holding that old card does not replace the Missouri license. Commercial drivers have their own rule. An out-of-state commercial driver who moved to Missouri within the last thirty days must obtain a Missouri license, and the details are explained in the separate commercial manual rather than in this guide. The instruction permit comes first at fifteen, the intermediate license follows at sixteen, and the full Class F license arrives at eighteen. Along the way we will see when the permit clock starts, why permits and licenses for younger drivers carry a special marking, and what the fee chart lists for each rung. Nothing forces you to replace it on your birthday. Notice that the age for this marking is twenty-one, not eighteen, so a driver can hold a full Class F license and still carry the minor marking if that card was issued before twenty-one.","fact_ids":["sec01-R12","sec01-R13"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":42,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u02-s6","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"What the fee chart lists","fact_ids":["sec01-F33","sec01-F36","sec01-F34","sec01-F35"]},"lines":[{"text":"Instruction permit: ten dollars, up to twelve months.","fact_ids":["sec01-F33","sec01-F36","sec01-F34","sec01-F35"]},{"text":"Intermediate: fourteen dollars, up to two years.","fact_ids":["sec01-F33","sec01-F36","sec01-F34","sec01-F35"]},{"text":"Full Class F: three-year or six-year terms.","fact_ids":["sec01-F33","sec01-F36","sec01-F34","sec01-F35"]}],"narration":{"text":"Now the prices on the fee chart. Each comes with different requirements, and the early one comes with firm limits on where, when and how you ride. The permit then comes with tight limits. You may ride in daylight only, within fifty miles of home, on a motorcycle of two hundred fifty cc or less, and with no passengers. Every one of those limits applies at the same time, on every ride.","fact_ids":["sec01-F09","sec01-F10"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":42,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u03-s4","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"The rider course age trap","fact_ids":["sec01-R02","sec01-F11"]},"lines":[{"text":"Course required only at fifteen and a half.","fact_ids":["sec01-R02","sec01-F11"]},{"text":"From sixteen: no course needed.","fact_ids":["sec01-R02","sec01-F11"]},{"text":"Written tests still apply without a license.","fact_ids":["sec01-R02","sec01-F11"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the trap with motorcycle permits. Many people assume every motorcycle permit requires a rider training course. It does not. Rider training is mandatory only for the motorcycle instruction permit taken at fifteen and a half. From age sixteen the rider training course is not required for a motorcycle instruction permit. That does not make the sixteen-year-old path test-free, though.
